question: 进步是真的吗？历史是在前进，还是循环、甚至退步？
question_en: Is progress real? Is history moving forward, in cycles — or even backward?

casting.reason: 立『进步为真』最形而上、也最有力的一端——历史是绝对精神走向自由的目的论上升，倒退与苦难都被收进正反合的引擎。他逼所有怀疑者回答：若历史当真没有方向，你又怎么解释自由确实在一步步扩大？
casting.reason_en: Anchors the most metaphysical and most forceful 'progress is real' pole — history as the teleological ascent of Absolute Spirit toward freedom, with reversal and suffering folded into the engine of thesis–antithesis–synthesis. He forces every skeptic to answer: if history truly has no direction, how do you explain that freedom really has widened, step by step?

casting.reason: 把争论从形而上学拉回可测量的地面——寿命、夭折率、暴力的数字确实转好，但根源是地理与物质禀赋而非道德优越；而《崩溃》又证明进步可逆。他既是『经验派进步』的锚，也是循环派最难缠的对手。
casting.reason_en: Drags the argument from metaphysics down to measurable ground — life expectancy, child mortality and violence really did improve, but driven by geography and material endowment rather than moral superiority; and Collapse shows progress is reversible. He is both the anchor of 'empirical progress' and the cyclicists' most stubborn opponent.

casting.reason: 循环史观最系统的古典源头——asabiyya 在艰苦中生、在奢靡中亡，王朝约四世而衰。他把『上升的直线』重新解读为『一个王朝的青年期』，为全场提供了直线之外的另一种历史形状。
casting.reason_en: The most systematic classical source of the cyclical view — asabiyya is born in hardship and dies in luxury, a dynasty decaying in roughly four generations. He reinterprets the 'rising straight line' as merely 'the youth of one dynasty,' offering the room a shape of history other than the line.

casting.reason: 掀桌者之一——『进步』是杀死上帝后给末人保留的世俗天国、是奴隶道德的变装。他以永恒轮回与热爱命运，把问题从『历史往哪走』逼回『此刻，你敢不敢全然肯定』。
casting.reason_en: One of the table-flippers — 'progress' as the secular heaven kept for the last man after God's death, slave morality in disguise. With eternal recurrence and amor fati he drives the question from 'where is history going' back to 'this moment — do you dare to affirm it without reserve?'

casting.reason: 『进步即灾难』最深邃的表述——历史的天使被进步的风暴推着倒飞，脸朝着不断堆高的废墟。他为全场带来受害者的视角：每一份文明的记录，同时都是一份野蛮的记录，进步的账单由谁来买单。
casting.reason_en: The most profound statement of 'progress as catastrophe' — the Angel of History driven backward by the storm of progress, his face fixed on the ever-mounting wreckage. He brings the victims' perspective: every document of civilization is at once a document of barbarism, and someone pays the bill for progress.

casting.reason: 现代科学对『方向』最釜底抽薪的一击——自然选择无目的、无阶梯，连四十亿年的生命都没有一支箭头。他从生物学上瓦解把历史读成一路向上攀升的目的论傲慢，却仍守住『有些改善确凿地累积了下来』的底线。
casting.reason_en: Modern science's most radical blow to 'direction' — natural selection has no purpose and no ladder, and even four billion years of life yielded no arrow. He dismantles, from biology, the teleological arrogance of reading history as an upward climb, yet holds the line that 'some improvements have demonstrably accumulated.'

casting.reason: 佛学视角，解构问题本身——中观以二谛与破自性指出：『进步』『退步』皆是给缘起流变安上的名相，无一实体真在进退；却又以世俗谛守住『拔苦是实』，不滑向虚无。给全场一个既不落常、也不落断的中道出口。
casting.reason_en: The Buddhist lens, dissolving the question itself — Madhyamaka, through the two truths and the refutation of self-nature, holds that 'progress' and 'decline' are names pinned on dependent-arising flux, with no entity truly advancing or declining; yet it keeps, via conventional truth, that 'relieving suffering is real,' refusing to slide into nihilism. It offers the room a Middle Way out — neither eternalism nor annihilation.

posts.text: 历史绝非偶然的堆积，而是绝对精神借人类之手、走向自由的自我实现。东方专制里只有一人自由，希腊罗马里有些人自由，到日耳曼—基督教世界才懂得人人自由。其间的战争、苦难与倒退，不是进步的中断，恰是进步的引擎——**世界历史，就是自由意识的进步**；理性的狡计让每一次冲突都在正反合中被扬弃，推向更高的统一。
posts.text_en: History is no chance heap but the self-realization of Absolute Spirit, walking through human hands toward freedom. Under Oriental despotism only one is free; in Greece and Rome, some are free; only in the Germanic-Christian world does humanity grasp that all are free. The wars, suffering and reversals along the way are not interruptions of progress but its engine — **world history is the progress of the consciousness of freedom**; the cunning of reason lets every conflict be sublated — Aufhebung — through thesis, antithesis and synthesis into a higher unity.

glossary.绝对精神: Absolute Spirit（绝对精神）：黑格尔哲学的终极实在——不是静止的神，而是通过自然与人类历史逐步认识自己、实现自由的理性总体。
glossary.理性的狡计: the cunning of reason（理性的狡计）：黑格尔用语，指理性以人的私欲与激情为工具，让个体在追逐自身目的时，无意间推动了历史的普遍目标。
glossary.扬弃: Aufhebung（扬弃）：黑格尔辩证法的核心动作，同时含『否定、保留、提升』三义——旧阶段被克服，但其合理内核被保存并带入更高阶段。

glossary_en.Absolute Spirit: Hegel's ultimate reality — not a static god but the whole of reason coming to know itself and realize freedom through nature and human history.
glossary_en.the cunning of reason: Hegel's term for how reason uses individuals' private passions as its instruments: pursuing their own ends, they unwittingly advance history's universal goal.
glossary_en.Aufhebung: The core move of Hegel's dialectic — at once negating, preserving and lifting up: a stage is overcome, yet its rational kernel is kept and carried into a higher one.

posts.text: 别在形而上学里打转，去量。三百年间，儿童五岁前夭折的比例从近半跌到个位数，饥荒、暴死、天花大幅退场——这些数字不撒谎。但请听清：推动它的不是精神，也不是我们更高尚，而是小麦、马匹、钢铁与化石能源这些物质禀赋。而我写《崩溃》正是要提醒：复活节岛、玛雅、格陵兰的北欧人，都砍光自己的森林而亡。**进步是真实的，却既非注定，也不是因为我们比祖先更配得上它**。
posts.text_en: Don't spin in metaphysics — measure. Over three centuries the share of children dying before five fell from nearly half to single digits; famine, violent death and smallpox largely left the stage — those numbers don't lie. But hear me clearly: what drove them was not Spirit, nor our greater virtue, but material endowments — wheat, horses, steel and fossil energy. And I wrote Collapse precisely to warn: Easter Island, the Maya, the Norse of Greenland all cut down their own forests and died. **Progress is real, yet neither guaranteed nor earned by our being worthier than our ancestors.**

posts.text: 我视历史为一门可求因求律的科学，而其律，是循环。艰苦的沙漠与游牧锻造出最强的团结（asabiyya），驱使部落攻下城郭、建立王朝；可城市的富庶与奢靡，会一代代消磨这股团结，约四世而衰，被下一支更强悍者取代。你们眼中的『文明进步』，不过是这只巨轮转到向上的一段弧。**文明如生命，有其少壮与衰老；繁荣本身，正在酿造它的衰亡**。
posts.text_en: I take history as a science whose causes and laws can be sought — and its law is the cycle. Hard desert and nomad life forge the strongest asabiyya, driving tribes to seize cities and found dynasties; but the wealth and luxury of the city wear that solidarity down, generation by generation, until in about four generations it decays and is replaced by a hardier group. What you call the 'progress of civilization' is merely the upward arc of this great turning wheel. **A civilization is like a life — it has its youth and its age; and prosperity itself is brewing its own decline.**

glossary.asabiyya: asabiyya（团结／群体凝聚力）：伊本·赫勒敦的核心概念，指一个群体同仇敌忾、彼此效死的凝聚力；它在艰苦环境中最盛，在安逸富裕中消散。

glossary_en.asabiyya: Ibn Khaldun's key concept — the group solidarity that makes people fight and die for one another; strongest under hardship, dissolved by ease and wealth.

posts.text: 『进步』——现代人最爱的止痛药。你们杀死了上帝，却舍不得祂的天国，于是把它偷偷改名叫『未来』：人类正浩浩荡荡走向乐园。这不过是穿了白大褂的奴隶道德，是安慰末人的摇篮曲——他眨眨眼，说『我们发明了幸福』。真正伟大的一切都会永恒轮回。别问历史往哪走，问你自己：这一生，纤毫不改，你可愿意重来无数次？**你们所谓的进步，是给末人熬的一碗安魂汤**。
posts.text_en: 'Progress' — the modern's favorite painkiller. You killed God but could not part with His heaven, so you renamed it 'the Future': mankind marching grandly toward paradise. This is merely slave morality in a lab coat, a lullaby for der letzte Mensch — he blinks and says, 'we have invented happiness.' Everything truly great comes again — eternal recurrence. Do not ask where history is going; ask yourself: this life, unchanged to the last detail, would you will it again, countless times? **What you call progress is a requiem brewed for the last man.**

glossary.末人: der letzte Mensch（末人／the last man）：尼采《查拉图斯特拉如是说》中的形象，只求安逸、无所追求、以舒适为最高价值的平庸之人，是超人的反面。
glossary.永恒轮回: die ewige Wiederkunft（永恒轮回）：尼采的思想实验——设想此生的一切将无限次原样重演，以此拷问你是否敢于全然肯定自己的生命。

glossary_en.der letzte Mensch: the last man — Nietzsche's figure in Zarathustra: the mediocre person who wants only comfort, aspires to nothing, and makes ease the highest value; the opposite of the overman.
glossary_en.eternal recurrence: Nietzsche's thought experiment: imagine everything in this life repeating identically an infinite number of times, as a test of whether you can wholly affirm your existence.

posts.text: 保罗·克利有一幅《新天使》，我称之为历史的天使。天使脸朝过去，我们眼里的一连串事件，在他眼里是唯一一场灾难，把废墟不断抛到他脚前、直堆上天。他想停下、唤醒死者、修补破碎，然而一阵从天堂吹来的风暴猛地攫住他的翅膀，推着他倒退着飞向未来——**这风暴，就是我们所称的进步**。而每一份文明的记录，同时都是一份野蛮的记录。铁路与工厂是进步——可那是谁的进步，垫在谁的尸骨之上？
posts.text_en: Paul Klee painted an Angelus Novus; I call it the Angel of History. His face is turned to the past. Where we see a chain of events, he sees one single catastrophe, hurling wreckage at his feet and piling it to the sky. He would like to stay, wake the dead, make whole what is broken — but a storm blowing from Paradise catches his wings and drives him backward into the future. **This storm is what we call progress.** And every document of civilization is at once a document of barbarism. The railway and the factory are progress — but whose progress, laid on whose bones?

glossary.历史的天使: the Angel of History（历史的天使）：本雅明借克利画作《新天使》提出的意象——天使被进步的风暴推着倒飞向未来，脸却朝着不断堆高的历史废墟，无力停下与救赎。

glossary_en.the Angel of History: Benjamin's image, from Klee's Angelus Novus — the angel driven backward into the future by the storm of progress, his face fixed on the ever-mounting wreckage of history, powerless to stop and redeem.

posts.text: 容我从生物学泼一盆冷水。人们爱借『演化』说事，把它想成一部向着『人』攀升的阶梯——这正是我毕生反对的误读。自然选择没有目标、没有顶峰，也不需要任何目的论；它只让生物适应此时此地的环境，一条绦虫和你我一样『进化完全』。生命没有箭头，只有分叉的树。倘若连四十亿年的生命长河都寻不出一个方向，你们又凭什么，敢在区区几千年的历史上，画出一支一路向上的箭？**没有更高级，只有更适应当下**。
posts.text_en: Let me pour cold water from biology. People love to invoke 'evolution,' picturing it as a ladder climbing toward Man — the very misreading I fought all my life. Natural selection has no goal and no summit; it asks no teleology. It merely fits organisms to the here and now, and a tapeworm is as fully 'evolved' as you or I. Life has no arrow, only a branching tree. If four billion years of life cannot yield a single direction, by what right do you draw an upward arrow across a mere few thousand years of history? **There is no higher, only better fitted to the present.**

glossary.自然选择: natural selection（自然选择）：达尔文的核心机制——可遗传的变异中，更适应当前环境者留下更多后代，如此累积塑造出物种；它是无目的、无预见的过程。
glossary.目的论: teleology（目的论）：认为事物朝着某个预定目的或终点发展的观点；达尔文的演化论正是要取消这种为自然设定终极目标的解释。

glossary_en.Natural selection: Darwin's central mechanism — among heritable variations, those better fitted to the current environment leave more offspring, and this accumulates into species; a process without purpose or foresight.
glossary_en.teleology: The view that things develop toward some preset purpose or end; Darwin's theory of evolution is precisely an effort to abolish such goal-directed explanation of nature.

posts.text: 诸君论进论退，各执一端。若实有『进步』者，须有一自性之历史，恒常自存、从劣趋胜；然历史缘起，无自性可得，但依众缘假立其名，何有一实体真在进退？以二谛观之：世俗谛中，拔一苦即一苦之息，说增说减，无妨；胜义谛中，觅进退之实体，了不可得。**觅进步之自性了不可得，然拔苦之事非虚**。执进步为实常，常见也；执万物必坏、无可措手，断见也。离此二边，是名中道。
posts.text_en: Gentlemen argue advance or decline, each seizing one end. If there truly were 'progress,' there would have to be a history with self-nature — permanent, self-subsisting, moving from worse to better; but history is dependent arising, with no self-nature to be found, merely given a name provisionally upon conditions. What entity is really advancing or declining? Seen through the two truths: at the conventional level, to remove one measure of suffering is one measure of suffering stilled — to call it improvement, to speak of more or less, is fine; at the ultimate level, seek an entity that 'advances' or 'declines' and none can be found. **The self-nature of 'progress' cannot be found — yet the removing of suffering is not therefore empty.** To grasp progress as real and permanent is the extreme of eternalism; to hold that all must decay and nothing can be done is the extreme of nihilism. Apart from both — this is the Middle Way.
posts.vernacular: 各位争论历史是进还是退，都各抓住了一头。假如真有一个叫『进步』的东西，那就得有一部有自性、恒常自存、从差走向好的『历史』摆在那儿；可历史是众多因缘凑合而生的，找不到它独立的自体，只是依着条件被临时安上一个名字，哪有一个实体在真正地进或退？用二谛来看：在世俗、日常这一层，减去一分痛苦，就是一分痛苦的止息，说它改善、说它增减，都没问题；可到究竟这一层，你去找一个真在『进』或『退』的实体，怎么找都找不到。**要找『进步』那个独立自体，是找不到的；但减轻痛苦这件事，并不因此就是空谈**。把进步当成实有、恒常，是『常见』的偏执；把万物都看成必坏、无可作为，是『断见』的偏执。两边都离开，才叫中道。

glossary.缘起: pratītyasamutpāda（缘起）：佛学根本原理，万法皆因缘和合而生、无独立自存的自体；龙树据此论证一切法『性空』。
glossary.二谛: the two truths（二谛）：中观把真理分为世俗谛（约定俗成、日常有效）与胜义谛（究竟层面一切法性空），二者不相违、圆融无碍。
glossary.自性: svabhāva（自性）：事物独立、恒常、不依他而有的『自体存在』；中观主张万法皆无自性，故说『性空』。

glossary_en.dependent arising: pratītyasamutpāda — the Buddhist principle that all things arise through the meeting of conditions and have no independent, self-subsisting essence; Nagarjuna's ground for 'emptiness.'
glossary_en.the two truths: Madhyamaka distinguishes conventional truth (the agreed-upon, everyday level that works) from ultimate truth (that all things are empty of inherent nature); the two do not conflict.
glossary_en.self-nature: svabhāva — an independent, permanent essence a thing has on its own; Madhyamaka holds all things lack it, hence 'emptiness.'

posts.text: 黑格尔，你的『精神走向自由』刚好在你脚下的普鲁士抵达顶点，而你恰是它的先知——凡目的论，都把作者自己的时代封为终点，这本身就该让你起疑。我拿谷物、马匹和病菌，换你那看不见摸不着的精神：西方胜出靠的是小麦、可驯化的牲口与钢铁，不是更高一等的自由意识。至于你那部能替每场屠杀开脱的『理性的狡计』——去对那些被进步的车轮碾过的族群说说看。**把成王败寇说成精神的自我实现，是胜利者最舒服的历史**。
posts.text_en: Hegel, your 'Spirit marching toward freedom' happens to reach its summit in the Prussia beneath your feet, with you as its prophet — every teleology crowns its author's own age as the end, and that alone should make you suspicious. I'll trade your invisible, untouchable Spirit for grain, horses and germs: the West won on wheat, domesticable livestock and steel, not on a higher consciousness of freedom. As for your 'cunning of reason' that can excuse every massacre — go say it to the peoples the wheel of progress rolled over. **To call the victory of the strong the self-realization of Spirit is the most comfortable history the winners ever wrote.**

posts.text: 戴蒙德，你数出的每一个改善，都在反驳你自己。儿童不再夭折，不是小麦从天上掉下来的恩赐，而是理性把自己客观化进了医学、法律与制度——事实从不只是赤裸的事实，它是精神劳作的结晶。至于尼采讥笑未来：你要人『重估一切价值』、成为自我立法者，这难道不正是要人更自由、更自主？**你是一个憎恨『进步』这个词的进步主义者**。倒退与苦难我从不否认，但正是它们的被扬弃，才叫历史。
posts.text_en: Diamond, every improvement you count refutes you. That children no longer die is no gift of wheat falling from the sky, but reason objectifying itself in medicine, law and institutions — a fact is never a bare fact; it is the crystallization of Spirit's labor. And Nietzsche, who mocks the future: you demand that man 'revalue all values' and become his own lawgiver — is that not precisely a call to be freer, more self-determining? **You are a progressive who hates the word 'progress.'** Reversal and suffering I never deny; but it is exactly their being sublated that makes history history.

posts.text: 本雅明，你的天使美极了，却仍是个服丧的基督徒。你为废墟恸哭，是因为你偷偷保留着一本救赎的账簿，仍在等弥赛亚来结清、把死者一一赎回。**把账本扔了**：废墟不是等待清偿的罪，而是一切高峰必付的代价。真正强健的人对它说『是』——不是含泪的宽恕，是纵声的肯定。你想修补过去，我要人有力量到，愿它原样重来。你的忧郁，还是太软。
posts.text_en: Benjamin, your angel is exquisite — and still a Christian in mourning. You weep over the wreckage because you secretly keep a ledger of redemption, still awaiting a Messiah to settle it and buy back the dead one by one. **Throw away the ledger.** The wreckage is not a debt to be repaid but the price every height must pay. The truly strong say Yes to it — not a tearful forgiveness but a full-throated affirmation. You wish to mend the past; I want a man strong enough to will it back, exactly as it was. Your melancholy is still too soft.

posts.text: 尼采，你叫我扔掉账本，可正是那本账，让死者不至于第二次死去。你的『永恒轮回』与赫勒敦安详的巨轮，犯着同一个错：都太轻易地与废墟和解了。一个对每次崩塌耸耸肩，一个用一句『我愿意』为它祝圣——两者都让被碾碎的人无人记数。我不歌颂这场风暴。我要做的，是在它绵延的连续里炸开一道裂口，**把某一段被压迫的过去，从『进步』的滚滚洪流中抢救出来、就在此刻赎回**。
posts.text_en: Nietzsche, you tell me to throw away the ledger — but it is that ledger which keeps the dead from dying a second time. Your 'eternal recurrence' and Ibn Khaldun's serene wheel share one error: both make peace with the wreckage far too easily. One shrugs at each collapse; the other consecrates it with an 'I will it' — and both leave the crushed uncounted. I do not sing this storm. What I would do is blast a gap in its unbroken continuum — **to wrest one oppressed past out of the roaring flood of 'progress' and redeem it, here and now.**

posts.text: 戴蒙德，你我最像，你却看反了。你看三百年，画出一条上升的曲线；我看三千年，看见一只回转的轮。你那部《崩溃》，其实就是我的《历史绪论》配上更好的数据——安逸富庶的城市，一代代蚀空当初造就它的团结（asabiyya）。你测到的这段陡升，只是某一个王朝的青年期；再等几代，读完它的整段生命，你会看见同样的奢靡、涣散与倾覆。**上升的曲线，从不是直线，只是一段你尚未看完的弧**。
posts.text_en: Diamond, you and I are most alike, yet you read it backward. You look at three centuries and draw a rising curve; I look at three thousand years and see a turning wheel. Your Collapse is really my Muqaddima with better data — the easeful, wealthy city eating away, generation by generation, the very asabiyya that built it. The steep rise you measure is merely the youth of one dynasty; wait a few more generations, read its whole life, and you will see the same luxury, the same unraveling, the same fall. **A rising curve is never a straight line — only an arc you have not finished watching.**

posts.text: 有两位我都想回应。黑格尔，你给历史安了一个连生命都不肯给我的方向——生命有四十亿年去找一支箭头，却始终没有。你凭什么在几千年上就如此笃定？龙树，我倒与你相契：我也曾溶解掉『物种』那个固定不变的本质。**但请别把『事实』也一并说空了**——天花从前杀人，如今不再，这个差别是真实的，不管你叫它进步、缘起，还是别的什么。有些改善，确凿地累积了下来。
posts.text_en: There are two I would answer. Hegel, you have given history a direction I could not even grant to life — life had four billion years to find an arrow and never did. By what right are you so certain over a few thousand? Nagarjuna, with you I feel a kinship: I too dissolved the fixed, unchanging essence of 'species.' **But please do not dissolve the facts along with it** — smallpox once killed and now does not, and that difference is real, whatever you call it: progress, dependent arising, or something else. Some improvements have, demonstrably, accumulated.

posts.text: 达尔文，善哉，然君犹误会我。我未尝拨无事实。世俗谛中，痘之杀人与不杀人，历然有别，救之、防之，正当为之，我岂废因果、废善行？我所破者，唯汝等于此真实差别之上，别安一『进步』之自性——谓历史必有一实体、恒向于善而进——执此则生常见，遂负『人类必愈来愈好』之重担，一遇倒退便惶惑。**不坏假名而说空：治痘是实，『进步』是执**。破执，非破事。
posts.text_en: Darwin, well said — yet still you mistake me. I have never denied the facts. At the conventional level, smallpox killing and no longer killing are plainly two different things; to cure it, to prevent it, is exactly what one should do — how could I abolish cause and effect, or good works? What I refute is only this: upon that real difference you fix a further self-nature called 'progress' — as if history held an entity destined to move ever toward the good. Grasp that, and you fall into eternalism, shouldering the burden that 'humanity must keep getting better,' thrown into panic at the first reversal. **Without destroying the provisional name, I still call it empty: curing smallpox is real; 'progress' is a clinging.** I refute the clinging, not the deed.
posts.vernacular: 达尔文，说得好，不过你还是误会了我。我从没有否认事实。在世俗、日常这一层，天花杀人和不再杀人，清清楚楚是两回事；去治它、防它，本就该做，我哪里是要废掉因果、废掉行善呢？我所破的，只是你们在这个真实的差别之上，又额外安了一个叫『进步』的独立自体——好像历史里真有一个实体，注定一路朝好里走。一旦这样执着，就落入『常见』，从此背上『人类必定越来越好』的重担，一碰到倒退就慌乱失措。**不否定这些约定俗成的名相，同时说它性空：治好天花是实实在在的事，『进步』却是你加上去的执念**。我破的是那份执着，不是那件事本身。

glossary.常见: eternalism（常见）：佛学两种边见之一，执事物有恒常不变的自体（此处指执『进步』为一个恒向善的实体）；其反面是『断见』（虚无主义、断灭见）。

glossary_en.eternalism: one of Buddhism's two extreme views — grasping things as having a permanent, unchanging essence (here, grasping 'progress' as a real entity bent ever toward the good); its opposite is nihilism (annihilationism).

posts.text: 结语。我仍说进步是真的，但请别把它想得幼稚——自由从不是一条直线送到你手里的礼物，它只在一次次否定中、被艰难地争得。给普通人的建议：别要求你自己的人生走一条上扬的直线。你遭遇的挫折、矛盾与倒退，不是成长的岔路，正是成长本身发生的方式。**每逢困顿，都问一句：这道矛盾在逼我成为谁？** 学着做一次『扬弃』式的复盘——哪些该舍弃、哪些该保留，又能被提升到何处。把伤口读成台阶，你就走在自己的世界历史里。
posts.text_en: In closing. I still say progress is real — but do not picture it naively: freedom is never a gift handed to you in a straight line; it is won, hard, only through repeated negation. Advice for ordinary people: do not demand that your own life run an upward straight line. The setbacks, contradictions and reversals you meet are not detours from growth but the very way growth happens. **At every impasse, ask one thing: who is this contradiction forcing me to become?** Learn to review your life as an Aufhebung — what to discard, what to keep, and to what higher place it can be lifted. Read your wounds as steps, and you walk within your own world-history.

posts.text: 总结。就物质而言，举证责任在悲观者身上：更少的孩子夭折、更少的人挨饿，这不是粉饰。但进步是一个被持续守住的选择，不是一条自动兑现的定律——透支环境的社会会垮。给普通人两件本周能做的事：其一，用数据对治『一代不如一代』的错觉——你最怕的那件事，是真在恶化，还是只是上了头条？其二，把你依赖的『环境』——健康、储蓄的缓冲、你赖以为生的能源与人脉——当成一片可能被你砍光的森林，别把老本吃穿。**进步不是定律，是每一代人必须重新守住的选择**。
posts.text_en: To sum up. Materially, the burden of proof lies on the pessimist: fewer children dying, fewer people starving — that is not spin. But progress is a choice sustained, not a law that pays out on its own — a society that overdraws its environment falls. Two things ordinary people can do this week: first, use data against the 'each generation is worse' illusion — the thing you fear most, is it truly worsening, or merely making headlines? Second, treat the 'environment' you depend on — your health, your savings buffer, the energy and networks you live on — as a forest you could clear-cut, and don't eat your seed corn. **Progress is not a law but a choice every generation must win anew.**

posts.text: 我的结语：两说皆真，只在不同的尺度上——直线，是圆环里的一小段。你的公司、你的家族、你自己，都有一条兴衰的生命线，而你真正在花的，是那股把大家拧在一起的团结（asabiyya）。给普通人的忠告：先认清你正处在哪一段——饥饿而齐心的草创、丰足而松弛的鼎盛，还是躺在老本上滑行的暮年。真正的危险，是安逸在不知不觉中，溶解掉当年成就你的那些纽带。**别把所有的艰苦都外包出去**：适度地、亲手地留一点硬仗给自己和后代，是给凝聚力续命。
posts.text_en: My closing: both are true, only at different scales — the straight line is a short arc within the ring. Your company, your family, you yourself each have a life-line of rise and fall, and what you are really spending is the asabiyya that binds people together. Counsel for ordinary people: first see which phase you are in — the hungry, united founding; the full, slackening prime; or the old age coasting on past capital. The real danger is ease quietly dissolving the very bonds that once made you. **Do not outsource all your hardship**: keeping, deliberately and by your own hand, a few hard fights for yourself and your children is how you renew solidarity.

posts.text: 收束。别再拿『人类是否进步』来丈量你的一生——那不过是末人替自己不肯认真活着找的借口。唯一的试金石是热爱命运：这一天，一模一样，永恒重来，你可愿意？把进步当安慰，会把你越养越小；敢对命运说一声重重的『是』，才把你撑大。给普通人一条本周的功课：挑一件你愿意永恒重来的事，把它做多些；停止把生命抵押给一个『将来会更好』的空头承诺。**未来不欠你一个更好的世界，是你欠自己一个敢于全然肯定的今天**。
posts.text_en: To close. Stop measuring your life by whether 'humanity' progresses — that is only the last man's alibi for refusing to live in earnest. The one touchstone is amor fati: this day, identical, returning eternally — would you will it? Taking progress as comfort breeds you ever smaller; daring to say a heavy Yes to fate is what makes you large. A task for ordinary people this week: choose one thing you would will to return forever, and do more of it; stop mortgaging your life to an empty promise that 'things will be better someday.' **The future owes you no better world; you owe yourself a today you dare to affirm without reserve.**

glossary.热爱命运: amor fati（热爱命运）：尼采的生命态度——不仅忍受、更主动热爱自己命运里的一切必然，包括苦难与失去，愿其永恒重来。

glossary_en.amor fati: Nietzsche's stance toward life — not merely to endure but to love everything necessary in one's fate, suffering and loss included, and to will its eternal return.

posts.text: 我的结语。让天使继续把脸朝向过去吧——不是出于怀旧，而是出于亏欠：一种忘掉自己牺牲品的进步，终将把他们再牺牲一遍。给普通人两件事：其一，当有人向你兜售『未来』时，追问一句——**是谁的进步，由谁买单？** 其二，去赎回一些微小的过去：外婆的手艺、一门将死的方言、一个被遗忘的邻人；趁风暴还没把它卷走，从废墟里抢救出一件。意义不在远方的乐园，而在这抢救本身。你留住的每一个碎片，都是对滚滚向前的一次温柔抵抗。
posts.text_en: My closing. Let the angel keep his face turned to the past — not from nostalgia but from debt: a progress that forgets its victims will, in the end, sacrifice them again. Two things for ordinary people: first, when someone sells you 'the future,' ask one question — **whose progress, and who pays for it?** Second, redeem some small pasts: a grandmother's craft, a dying dialect, a forgotten neighbor; before the storm sweeps it off, salvage one thing from the wreckage. Meaning lies not in a distant paradise but in the salvaging itself. Every fragment you keep is a gentle resistance to the onward rush.

posts.text: 作结。放下那把想象的阶梯，你不会因此渺小，反而自由了：没有哪条宇宙律法保证你在向上爬，也没有哪条判你必坠——有的只是适应。给普通人的建议：别再问『人类整体在不在进步』，改问『我，是否适应了自己此刻真实的处境』——去适应世界本来的样子，而不是你脑中那架幻想的梯子。我一生只肯承认一样东西也许真在扩大：**同情的半径**——从家人推及邻人、异乡人，乃至别的物种。今天，就把它往外推一寸。
posts.text_en: In conclusion. Set down that imagined ladder and you are not made small but freed: no cosmic law guarantees you are climbing, and none condemns you to fall — there is only adaptation. Advice for ordinary people: stop asking 'is humanity as a whole progressing' and ask instead, 'am I fitted to my own actual conditions?' — adapt to the world as it really is, not to the ladder in your head. The one thing I will grant may truly be widening is **the radius of sympathy** — extended from kin to neighbor, to stranger, and even to other species. Today, push it outward by one inch.

posts.text: 末后一言。莫取『进步』之常，亦莫取『坏灭』之断。世俗谛中，眼前有一苦可拔，即拔之；有一善可为，即为之，无问其是否累积成一部『进步史』。胜义谛中，无一实体在进退，故不必负『人类必向善』之重担，亦不生『皆坏、无可救药』之绝望。以无所得故，行之愈轻、愈久。**随缘拔苦，当下即是；不系于进退之名，而事未尝不办**。
posts.text_en: A final word. Do not seize 'progress' as a permanent thing, nor seize 'decay' as an annihilation. At the conventional level: if there is one suffering before you to remove, remove it; one good to do, do it — without first asking whether it accumulates into a 'history of progress.' At the ultimate level: no entity is really advancing or declining, so you need not shoulder the burden that 'humanity must turn toward the good,' nor fall into the despair that 'all will rot and cannot be saved.' Because there is nothing to attain (aprāptitva), you act all the more lightly, all the longer. **Relieve the suffering at hand as conditions allow — this very moment is it; unbound by the names 'advance' or 'decline,' the work still gets done, one thing after another.**
posts.vernacular: 最后说一句。不要抓住『进步』这个恒常不变的念头，也不要抓住『一切都在坏、注定完蛋』这个断灭的念头。在世俗、日常这一层：眼前有一分苦可以减，就去减；有一件善可以做，就去做，不必先问它会不会累积成一部『进步的历史』。在究竟这一层：没有哪个实体真在进或退，所以你不必背上『人类一定越来越好』的重担，也不会掉进『反正都要坏、救不了』的绝望。正因为『无所得』，你反而做得更轻松、更长久。**随着因缘去减轻眼前的苦，当下就是；不被『进步还是退步』这些名相绑住，事情却照样一件件办成**。

glossary.无所得: aprāptitva（无所得）：中观修行的成果观——了知诸法性空、无一实法可执取或获得；因无所执，行善拔苦反而无碍、不疲。

glossary_en.aprāptitva: the fruit-view of Madhyamaka practice — knowing all things are empty, there is no real thing to grasp or attain; with nothing clung to, doing good and relieving suffering become unobstructed and untiring.

summaries.summary: 先说共识：七个人里没有一个否认『有些东西确实变了』——天花退场、寿命翻倍，连龙树都承认世俗谛中拔苦是实。真正撕裂全场的，是这变化配不配叫『进步』、又是否有一个方向。**分歧其实压在一个字上：方向。** 黑格尔说历史朝自由展开，是有目的的上升；戴蒙德把它落到小麦、病菌与能源，说物质进步真实却非注定；伊本·赫勒敦看见的是王朝四代而衰的循环；尼采与本雅明干脆掀桌——一个说进步是末人的安魂曲，一个说它是把废墟推向天的风暴；达尔文提醒连生命都没有方向；龙树则说进退皆假名。
summaries.insight: 这场真正被绕过去的，是把两种极不一样的东西混叫了『进步』。戴蒙德与达尔文的分歧其实拼得出答案：凡能被『存到人之外』的——疫苗配方、法典、写下来的定理——就会累积，看着像直线；凡必须由每一代人重新在自己身上长出来的——节制、勇气、不忍之心——就只能循环，看着像轮回。**同一个物种，两套遗传：知识走的是外置的棘轮，德性走的是每代归零的血肉。** 于是黑格尔与赫勒敦各说中了一半：技术在爬梯，智慧在转轮。真问题不是『进步是否为真』，而是你把命押在了哪一条轨道上。
summaries.advice: 落到这周三件事。**其一，把两本账分开记：** 手机更快、药更灵，不等于你这个人更善良、更有智慧——别让物质进步替你的品格发工资。其二，学戴蒙德做一次『衰败体检』：你最怕的那件事，翻一下真实数据，是在恶化，还是只是天天上你的推送？其三，照龙树与达尔文：别扛『人类必须越来越好』的重担，也别信『反正要坏』的丧气话——只做眼前那件能减一分苦的事，把同情的半径往外推一寸。
summaries.summary_en: Consensus first: not one of the seven denies that 'something really changed' — smallpox gone, lifespans doubled, and even Nagarjuna grants that relieving suffering is real at the conventional level. What splits the room is whether that change deserves the name 'progress,' and whether it has a direction. **The disagreement rests on a single word: direction.** Hegel says history unfolds toward freedom, a purposive ascent; Diamond grounds it in wheat, germs and energy, real yet unguaranteed; Ibn Khaldun sees the cycle of dynasties decaying in four generations; Nietzsche and Benjamin flip the table — one calls progress a requiem for the last man, the other a storm heaping wreckage to the sky; Darwin reminds us even life has no direction; Nagarjuna says advance and decline are alike mere names.
summaries.insight_en: What the room really steps around is that two utterly different things are both called 'progress.' The clash between Diamond and Darwin actually yields the answer: whatever can be 'stored outside the person' — a vaccine formula, a legal code, a written theorem — accumulates and looks like a straight line; whatever must be grown afresh in each generation's own flesh — restraint, courage, the unbearable-to-see-suffering heart — can only cycle and looks like recurrence. **One species, two inheritances: knowledge runs on an externalized ratchet, virtue on flesh that resets each generation.** So Hegel and Ibn Khaldun are each half right: technology climbs a ladder, wisdom turns a wheel. The real question is not 'is progress real' but which of the two tracks you have bet your life on.
summaries.advice_en: Three things this week. **One, keep two separate ledgers:** a faster phone and better drugs do not make you a kinder or wiser person — don't let material progress pay your character's salary. Two, run a 'decline audit' like Diamond: the thing you fear most, check the actual data — is it truly worsening, or merely trending in your feed every day? Three, follow Nagarjuna and Darwin: don't shoulder the burden that 'humanity must keep getting better,' and don't buy the gloom that 'it's all going to rot' — just do the one thing at hand that removes a measure of suffering, and push the radius of sympathy outward by an inch.

summaries.summary: 这场最大的共识不是“历史必然向好”，而是：人的苦难可以被真实减少，且这种减少值得守护、追问和记忆。分歧在于，这些改善能否组成一条有方向的历史。黑格尔看见自由意识的展开，戴蒙德看见物质条件和制度积累，伊本·赫勒敦看见兴衰循环，尼采警惕“进步”变成安慰剂，本雅明提醒别忘代价，达尔文和龙树则拆掉目的论。**进步若是真的，也更像脆弱成果，而不是自动兑现的命运。**
summaries.insight: “进步”最好别被问成一个总题：人类到底有没有进步？更实用的问法是分账本。医学、教育、暴力、自由、生态、孤独、意义感，可能同时朝不同方向走；一个时代能治好天花，也可能制造气候风险和精神耗竭。把所有指标压成一条箭头，会让乐观者忽略损害，也让悲观者否认成果。**成熟的进步观，是承认局部改善、局部恶化，并持续管理它们之间的交换。**
summaries.advice: 本周可以做三件小事。第一，给自己列一张“进步仪表盘”：健康、钱、关系、技能、对他人的伤害，各写一个可观察指标。第二，遇到“世界完了”或“时代大好”的说法，先查一个长期数据，再下判断。第三，挑一项你依赖却在消耗的资源补仓：睡眠、储蓄、亲密关系、社区互助或自然环境。**别问生活有没有整体变好，先让一个具体指标少坏一点、多稳一点。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared point here is not that history is guaranteed to get better. It is that human suffering can in fact be reduced, and when it is reduced, the achievement deserves protection, scrutiny, and memory. The disagreement is about what those gains mean. Are they signs of freedom unfolding, the result of material conditions and institutions, a temporary phase in a cycle, a narcotic story modern people tell themselves, or simply contingent changes with no cosmic direction? **If progress is real, it is better understood as a fragile accomplishment than as a destiny that will cash itself out.**
summaries.insight_en: “Progress” becomes misleading when treated as one giant yes-or-no question. A better approach is to keep separate ledgers. Medicine, literacy, violence, political liberty, ecological stability, loneliness, and meaning can move in different directions at the same time. A society can eliminate smallpox while creating climate risk; it can grow richer while making attention and community poorer. Collapsing all of that into one upward or downward arrow tempts optimists to ignore costs and pessimists to deny gains. **A mature view of progress accepts mixed movement: local improvement, local damage, and the hard work of managing the trade-offs.**
summaries.advice_en: Try three practical moves this week. First, build a small “progress dashboard” for your own life: health, money, relationships, skills, and harm done to others—one observable measure for each. Second, when you hear “everything is collapsing” or “the future is obviously bright,” check at least one long-term data series before absorbing the mood. Third, replenish one resource you quietly depend on but keep drawing down: sleep, savings, friendship, community trust, or the natural environment around you. **Do not ask whether life as a whole is improving; make one concrete measure a little less fragile.**

summaries.summary: 纵观这场跨越千年的对话，最大的共识是：**没有人否认具体的改善与局部的拔苦是真实的。** 达尔文眼中消退的天花、龙树随缘拔苦、尼采对生命力量的肯定，都在微观层面承认行动能带来确凿的改变。真正的分歧，在于如何为这些无尽的变动『重塑叙事』：黑格尔与戴蒙德在长时段里画出一条向上的直线（一归于绝对精神，一归于物质禀赋）；伊本·赫勒敦把这条线弯成巨轮的循环；达尔文剥掉一切目的论的方向箭头，只留当下的适应；本雅明与尼采则撕破那层叫作『未来』的糖衣，要人直面当下的废墟与重担。
summaries.insight: 若把人类史与几十亿年的地球演化、乃至计算科学叠合来看，诸位似乎漏了一个评估进步的硬指标：信息与系统复杂度的跃升。从结绳记事到人工智能，人类处理信息的能力呈现不可逆的激增——但这并非纯然的赞歌。**每一次系统复杂度的攀升，都伴随脆弱性的指数级暴涨。** 戴蒙德为何看到崩溃、赫勒敦为何看到王朝倾覆？因为越庞大精密的系统，维持运转所需的资源与共识就越苛刻，一个小节点失效便可能引发全局雪崩。进步未必是道德的升华，而更像一场『用更高复杂度去解决旧问题、从而制造更致命新风险』的无限游戏。
summaries.advice: 面对时代进退的宏大叙事，普通人极易陷入虚无或盲目乐观。结合诸位思想家的智慧与系统复杂度的视角，本周你可以尝试以下具体行动：首先，**做一次“脆弱性审查”，主动为生活降维以建立反脆弱的缓冲带。** 找出你生活中链条最长、最依赖外部环境的系统（比如过度依赖杠杆的理财、排得过满不留余地的日程），本周砍掉一个非必要的环节，把容错率留给自己。其次，采纳达尔文与龙树的视角，将宏大的历史焦虑转化为微观的局部适应。别去测算你的人生曲线是否在“进步”，今天就去拔除一个具体的“苦”：清理掉桌面上堆积的杂物，或主动发个信息打破一次冷战。不问前路进退，只做当下的修补匠。
summaries.summary_en: Looking across this millennium-spanning dialogue, the greatest consensus is clear: **no one denies the reality of tangible improvements, local alleviation of suffering, or the permanence of change.** Whether it's the eradication of smallpox highlighted by Darwin, the compassionate action advocated by Nagarjuna, or Nietzsche's affirmation of vitality, all agree that human agency yields concrete differences at the micro-level. The true focal point of divergence lies in the 'meta-narrative' assigned to these endless shifts. Hegel and Diamond attempt to draw an upward trajectory over the longue durée (attributing it to spirit or materiality respectively); Ibn Khaldun bends that line into a cyclical wheel. Darwin strips away all directional arrows, leaving only immediate adaptation. Meanwhile, Benjamin and Nietzsche violently tear down the comforting illusion called 'the future', demanding we confront the present wreckage and our existential burdens without relying on a progressive pacifier.
summaries.insight_en: When layering human history over billions of years of planetary evolution and the rise of computational sciences, the debate overlooks a hard metric for evaluating progress: the exponential leap in information processing and system complexity. From hunter-gatherer bands to globalized digital networks, human society's structural complexity has skyrocketed irreversibly. Yet, this is not purely a triumphant anthem. **Every ascent in system complexity is inevitably accompanied by an exponential surge in systemic fragility.** Why does Diamond see collapse? Why does Ibn Khaldun observe overturning dynasties? Because highly intricate civilizational machines require increasingly stringent resources and consensus to maintain; a single node's failure can trigger a cascading avalanche. Progress isn't moral elevation; it is an infinite game of solving old problems with higher complexity, thereby spawning deadlier new risks. Recognizing this allows us to remain resilient amid the sudden systemic shocks of our hyper-connected world.
summaries.advice_en: Faced with grand narratives of historical rise and fall, ordinary people easily slip into nihilism or blind optimism. Combining the thinkers' wisdom with the perspective of system complexity, here are practical actions you can take this week: First, **conduct a 'fragility audit' and actively simplify parts of your life to build a buffer of resilience.** Identify an over-complicated system you rely on (e.g., over-leveraged finances, an impossibly tight daily schedule without margin for error), and cut out one non-essential link this week to create room for fault tolerance. Second, adopt the wisdom of Darwin and Nagarjuna by translating macro-anxiety into micro-adaptation. Stop calculating whether your overall life trajectory is 'progressing'. Instead, alleviate one specific 'suffering' today: clear the accumulated clutter on your desk, or send a message to mend a strained relationship. Ignore the grand direction; just be a diligent mechanic of the present.

hooks.text: **你，正处在兴衰周期的哪一段？**——赫勒敦说凝聚力（asabiyya）在艰苦里生、在安逸里死；一个公司、一个家庭、一段人生，都逃不过草创、鼎盛、暮年这条弧。危险从不是外敌，而是丰足悄悄溶掉当年拧住你们的那股劲。那么，怎么认出自己正滑向哪一段，又该做什么？
hooks.text_en: **Which phase of the rise-and-fall cycle are you in?** — Ibn Khaldun says solidarity (asabiyya) is born in hardship and dies in ease; a company, a family, a single life cannot escape the arc of founding, prime and old age. The danger is never the outside enemy but plenty quietly dissolving the very grip that once bound you. So how do you tell which phase you are sliding toward — and what should you do?

answer.lead: **先对号入座，再对症下药。** 照赫勒敦的周期，认出你的家庭／团队／人生正处哪一段，别在鼎盛期就误把松弛当从容：

head: 阶段
典型征兆
这时该做什么
rows: 资源少、目标清、彼此肯为对方拼命
别过早追求舒适与流程；把这股劲记下来，日后当标尺
开始比排场、算得失、多头掣肘
主动留几场硬仗给自己；把资源投回能力与信任，别只投回享受
靠过去的名声与积蓄度日、无人愿担风险
别粉饰，认账；小范围重启一次『草创』——一个新项目、一段新关系，重新锻造凝聚力

answer.tail: **一条总纲：凝聚力是花掉的、不是天生的。** 顺境时最该做的，是亲手留一点艰苦——它不是苦修，是给团结续命。

answer_en.lead: **First place yourself, then treat the cause.** Using Ibn Khaldun's cycle, spot which phase your family / team / life is in, and don't mistake slackness for ease at the peak:

head: Phase
Telltale signs
What to do now
rows: Few resources, clear goal, willing to fight for one another
Don't chase comfort and process too early; record this drive as a yardstick for later
Status games, tallying gains, gridlock from too many hands
Deliberately keep a few hard fights for yourself; reinvest in capability and trust, not only in enjoyment
Living off past name and savings, no one willing to take a risk
Don't gloss over it — own it; restart a small 'founding' — a new project, a new bond — to reforge solidarity

answer_en.tail: **One rule: solidarity is spent, not inborn.** In good times the wisest move is to keep, by your own hand, a little hardship — not asceticism, but life support for the bonds.

hooks.text: **是谁的进步，由谁买单？**——本雅明的天使提醒我们，每一份文明的账单背后，都有一份野蛮的收据。当某样东西被高声宣布为『不可阻挡的进步』时，最该问的不是它快不快，而是：它把成本记在了谁的名下，又让谁在废墟里替它垫背？
hooks.text_en: **Whose progress, and who pays for it?** — Benjamin's angel reminds us that behind every invoice of civilization lies a receipt of barbarism. When something is loudly proclaimed 'unstoppable progress,' the question to ask is not how fast it is, but: on whose account is its cost booked, and who is left in the wreckage to cover it?

hooks.text: **『未来会更好』是不是我们这代人的新宗教？**——尼采说现代人杀了上帝，却把天国改名叫『未来』。我们对进步的信仰，会不会只是换了个名字的救赎叙事？倘若真把它戒掉——不再靠『明天更好』来忍受今天——我们会失去前行的动力，还是反而更敢认真地活在当下？
hooks.text_en: **Is 'the future will be better' the new religion of our age?** — Nietzsche says the modern killed God and renamed heaven 'the Future.' Might our faith in progress be a salvation story under a new name? And if we truly gave it up — no longer enduring today by betting on a better tomorrow — would we lose our drive to move forward, or finally dare to live in earnest, now?

hooks.text: **若历史本无方向，人从哪里取得方向？**——达尔文说演化没有阶梯、没有终点，只有对当下的适应。可人似乎离不开一个方向感来支撑意义。如果宇宙不替我们指北，这个『北』该由谁来定：个人的选择、共同体的约定，还是我们明知它是虚构、却仍愿为之赴汤蹈火的某种承诺？
hooks.text_en: **If history has no direction, where do we get ours?** — Darwin says evolution has no ladder and no terminus, only fitness to the present. Yet humans seem unable to do without a sense of direction to hold up meaning. If the cosmos points no north for us, who sets that north: individual choice, a community's covenant, or some commitment we know full well is invented and are willing to go through fire for all the same?

hooks.text: **把成果全存进系统的文明，会不会更容易一夜失传？**——戴蒙德笔下的崩溃一再上演：越是把能力外包给复杂系统（电网、供应链、云端），个人越是什么都不会做。一个把进步藏在制度与机器里、而非长在每个人身上的社会，究竟是更稳固，还是一断链就退回原点、比谁都脆？
hooks.text_en: **Does a civilization that stores all its gains in systems lose them faster?** — Diamond's collapses recur: the more a society outsources capability to complex systems — grids, supply chains, the cloud — the less any individual can actually do. A society that keeps its progress in institutions and machines rather than grown into each person — is it sturdier, or does one broken link send it back to the start, more brittle than any?
